pl-l3d37c3-d1e112.summary: Explains that the Church received the gift that remission of sins happens in the Holy Spirit: though the Trinity does it, it belongs properly to the Spirit, since he is the Spirit of adoption, the Love and bond or communion of Father and Son; hence our justification and rest are often attributed to him.
claims: Remission of sins is done by the Trinity but attributed properly to the Holy Spirit.
The Spirit is the Love and bond of Father and Son.

pl-l3d37c3-d1e121.summary: States that these are the three precepts of the first tablet concerning God: the first, on worshipping one God, pertains to the Father, in whom is unity or authority; the second to the Son, in whom is equality; the third to the Holy Spirit, in whom is the communion of both.
claims: The three precepts of the first tablet correspond to Father, Son, and Spirit.

pl-l3d37c3-d1e124.summary: Heading-like line introducing the commandments of the second tablet.

pl-l3d37c3-d1e130.summary: States that the second tablet had seven commandments pertaining to love of neighbor.
claims: The second tablet has seven commandments.

pl-l3d37c3-d1e135.summary: Gives the first precept of the second tablet, referring to one's earthly father as the first of the first tablet to the heavenly Father: honor your father and mother, that you may live long in the land of the living. Parents are honored by showing them due reverence and supplying their needs.
claims: Honoring parents corresponds to honoring the heavenly Father.
Honoring parents means reverence and support.

pl-l3d37c3-d1e144.summary: Gives the second precept, 'you shall not kill': literally it forbids the act of murder, spiritually also the will to kill; so the Gospel adds to the letter of this commandment, expressing in its letter what the letter of the Law did not.
claims: Literally the precept forbids the act of killing; spiritually the will.
The Gospel's letter expresses the spiritual sense of the Law.

pl-l3d37c3.summary: Explains that the remission of sins, though done by the Trinity, belongs properly to the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of adoption and the Love and bond of Father and Son, to whom justification and rest are often attributed. The three precepts of the first tablet correspond to the persons: one God worshipped to the Father, of unity and authority; the second to the Son, of equality; the third to the Spirit, of communion. The second tablet has seven precepts on love of neighbor. The first, honoring parents, corresponds to the first of the first tablet, the heavenly Father: parents are owed reverence and the necessities of life. The second, 'you shall not kill', forbids the act literally and the will to kill spiritually, which the Gospel makes explicit.
claims: The remission of sins is attributed properly to the Holy Spirit, though done by the Trinity.
The three precepts of the first tablet correspond to Father, Son, and Spirit.
The second tablet has seven precepts on love of neighbor.
Honoring parents means reverence and support.
'You shall not kill' spiritually forbids the will to kill.
